chunks: What Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that he was asked about the newborn, so long as the pen has not begun to run upon him, whether prayer is performed over him. He said:
No; rather, the prayer is only upon the man and the woman when the pen has begun to run upon them.

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: an adult male subject to the ruling
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the funeral prayer being discussed in this ruling
key_terms.الْقَلَمُ: a metaphor for the onset of legal accountability and obligation
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: an adult female subject to the ruling
key_terms.الْمَوْلُودِ: the newborn child about whom the question is asked
key_terms.عَلَيْهِمَا: upon the two, referring to the man and the woman
key_terms.يُصَلَّى: to have the funeral prayer performed over someone

ai.seo_question: Is salat performed over a newborn before legal accountability begins?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the funeral prayer for a newborn child. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that the prayer is only for a male or female upon whom the pen has begun to run, meaning one who has reached the stage of legal accountability.
